summary: Ask deadlines follow the asked person's deadline clock, and an ask's priority decides urgency: `work ask --priority`, and an `urgent` flag on attention rows

replay.detail: No projection changes. Effective deadlines are computed at read time from the ask and the person's person.deadline-clock-set claims; a person-step row's priority is read from its work.person-asked claim.

schema.detail: work.person-asked claims now carry the optional `priority` field that the claim registry already declares (critical, high or low; normal is not recorded). The client-v0 Attention resource gains the optional boolean `urgent`; the Rust, Swift (`urgent: Bool?`) and TypeScript clients are regenerated. PersonAskRequest gains an optional `priority`.

rules.detail: An ask's effective deadline is its stored deadline plus the time the asked person held their deadline clock since it was asked: hold-all holds every ask, hold-routine only asks that are not urgent. Urgent is one server rule: an ask with priority critical, whatever its deadline; attention rows now expose it as urgent. While an open hold applies, no default fires and no wake is armed. The reconciler, the person's home deadline_at and the late-answer stale-fence all use the effective deadline, so an answer stored after the stored deadline but before the effective one is accepted and beats the default. Browser pairing requests always expire on time. A retry under the same idempotency key must name the same priority; an unknown priority, or one other than normal on an update, is refused with invalid-ask-priority. The person-step row's priority is the ask's (normal without one); every attention row carries urgent.

compatibility.detail: Mixed versions: an ask resolves only on its origin member, so an origin on an older build ignores holds and applies the default at the stored deadline until it upgrades; a newer member may then accept an answer the older origin would fence, and the members keep different standing responses until both run this build. Clients: urgent is absent from older daemons and reads as not urgent. Roll daemons before `work ask --priority` callers: an older daemon ignores the priority field, so a critical ask it records is routine.

downtime.detail: No startup migration or service interruption.

manual.detail: No operator action. Asks are unaffected until a person sets a deadline-clock hold.

recovery.detail: Rolling back restores stored-deadline resolution; clock claims stay recorded and take effect again after re-upgrading.
